misconceptions.description: Believing that a GitHub Pages repository is private or safe to store credentials in just because the project looks unfinished or unlisted
misconceptions.trigger: learner commits an API key, password, or .env file into a public repo and assumes nobody will see it
misconceptions.feedback: GitHub Pages repos are public by default. Anything you commit, including secrets in old commits, is visible. Put keys in environment variables and add them to .gitignore before the first commit.

misconceptions.description: Thinking that deleting a sensitive file in a later commit removes it from the project history
misconceptions.trigger: learner deletes a leaked file and re-commits, expecting the data to be unrecoverable
misconceptions.feedback: A deleted file still lives in earlier commits. Reviewers can check out an old commit and read it. Rotate the leaked credential and rewrite history if it was ever pushed.

misconceptions.description: Pasting a full roster, gradebook, or personal dataset into an AI tool to get help formatting it
misconceptions.trigger: learner copies real names, emails, or IDs into a chatbot prompt
misconceptions.feedback: Strip or fake the personal columns first. Send the AI tool the structure and two anonymized sample rows, not the live data.
